epic.intent:
Make Dark Mechanicus the measurable planning and improvement loop for the owner's personal repositories. Each ticket, sprint report and epic exposes an explainable letter-grade scorecard grounded in SPACE, observed token usage and execution time. Retrospectives identify evidence-backed inefficiencies and create reviewable corrective work for the source repository or a locally available Dark Mechanicus source checkout.

Confirmed preference: BALANCED scoring. The five SPACE dimensions plus time efficiency and token efficiency have equal base influence (seven components, 1/7 each). SPACE supplies the multidimensional framework; the normalization and letter bands are an explicit, versioned Dark Mechanicus policy, not a validated scientific benchmark or official SPACE grade. Show all dimensions and outcome status beside the overall grade.

Initial policy: S is optional human satisfaction/confidence feedback (one brief sprint-level response may be explicitly shared as context, with ticket override); P is verified behavior/checks and attributable regressions; A is delivery against frozen committed scope with raw activity shown only as context; C is the reliability of handoffs and review evidence; E is corrective-work/flow efficiency, avoiding a second token/time charge. Token/time comparisons use a pre-dispatch budget or eligible frozen baseline. A/B/C/D/F bands begin at 90/80/70/60/<60. Missing observations are never zero or perfect. Final grades require complete required measurements and verified acceptance; otherwise show provisional/ungraded with coverage and effective weights. Confirmed failed mandatory outcomes cap the letter at F regardless of speed or token savings.

Reuse existing attempts, evidence, tier facts, report revisions, retro/redraft and human checkpoint approval. Preserve completed epics and approved reports: later defects, new measurements and policy versions produce labeled reassessments rather than rewriting history. Include all retries, rejected/failed/canceled/superseded attempts and coordination/verification overhead in resource totals; exclude duplicated carried-forward work. Distinguish wall time, active execution and parallel aggregate effort.

Retrospective actions become structured experiments: finding and source evidence, hypothesis, destination, proposed work, baseline metric, expected improvement, quality guardrail and later comparison. Same-repo work becomes a future sprint of an unfinished epic or a linked follow-up epic for completed work. Cross-repo work gets its own plan/branch/run and cross-repository provenance. The owner reviews the draft and uses normal run and checkpoint controls; a low grade never silently launches work. An installed DM app alone is not a source checkout, and missing source is explicitly unavailable.

Planning only. Implementation must not touch the in-flight Agents epic or share its checkout. Start from an integrated base when executed. Reuse agent usage hooks if available; external-host MCP observation input must work independently. No SaaS, tracker integrations, automatic cloning, automatic deployment/self-update, or fabricated provider usage.

successCriteria.text: Ticket scorecards expose all five SPACE dimensions, measured tokens and time, an explainable balanced seven-component A–F grade, evidence, coverage, policy/baseline versions and explicit failed/provisional/ungraded outcomes; reproducible cases prove low costs cannot hide failed mandatory outcomes.

Token and timing observations are attributed to attempts, tickets, sprints and runs without duplicates; retries and overhead are included, unknown usage remains unknown, cumulative and delta/provider token categories are normalized, and queue/human/blocked waits are distinguished from active execution.

Dedicated Scorecard tabs on tickets, epics and sprint reports show grades, dimension breakdowns, totals, original-scope delivery, failure/rework causes and comparable prior-wave changes; historical/legacy/in-flight views remain usable and never fabricate a complete grade.

Approved sprint scorecards and retros are reproducible from immutable input/policy/cutoff snapshots that survive export, clone/import and restart; later regressions or rescoring create dated reassessments without altering approved evidence or reopening completed epics.

Retrospectives center on observed scorecard gaps and structured improvement experiments; selecting actions previews and creates a valid corrective future sprint or same-repository follow-up epic with criteria, dependencies, provenance, Fireguard and an acceptance node.

Corrective actions can target the active repository or an owner-selected verified local Dark Mechanicus source checkout, using separate target-owned plans, branches and runs with durable cross-repo links, recoverable/idempotent writes, existing authorization and human checkpoints; an unavailable target never silently redirects work.

An end-to-end two-repository exercise demonstrates measurement → grades in all three tabs → retrospective → approved corrective work → before/after assessment, including legacy/missing data and failed/retried paths, with documentation and the repository's normal delivery checks.

epic.title: SPACE scorecards: balanced grades, token and time accounting, and corrective retrospectives

bundle.rationale: Planning only; do not start this epic. Five milestones: trustworthy measurements → balanced grading/snapshots → three scorecard tabs → score-driven same-repo correction → optional local Dark Mechanicus target and end-to-end verification. User explicitly selected balanced weights. Each sprint has five implementation/design/documentation work tickets, one dedicated Fireguard ticket and one acceptance node covering every work ticket. Real dependencies permit independent work at cap 2; shared-file edits serialize under the orchestrator. Profiles follow existing core/UI presets with explicit size/effort and no forced model. Critical path: contract→ledger→ingestion/timing→usage→metrics→grader→snapshot→API/tabs→experiments→corrective draft→destination broker→UI→guides/E2E. Human approval at every checkpoint. Execute from an isolated codex/space-scorecards branch on an integrated base; do not switch or modify the currently active Agents epic. Adapter integration must reuse its available source interfaces, while external MCP telemetry is independently supported. The final grade is a product policy, not a claim that Scrum/SPACE causally improves agents. Reference: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/publication/the-space-of-developer-productivity-theres-more-to-it-than-you-think/

acceptanceCriteria.text: Typed policy, observation, baseline, grade and evidence contracts define units, scope, source, observed/estimated/missing states and stable IDs; representative serialized fixtures validate.
The initial rubric specifies deterministic 0–100 normalization, equal 1/7 base weights, A≥90/B≥80/C≥70/D≥60/F<60, precision before display rounding, and worked complete/sparse/failure examples.

Missing required verification yields Ungraded; confirmed mandatory failure caps F; incomplete other factors yield explicitly Provisional or Ungraded with coverage and effective weights, never imputed success.

Token/time scoring requires a frozen pre-dispatch budget or comparable prior cohort identified by task type/size/risk and sample size; no eligible baseline is missing, and editing a budget cannot improve an already executing assessment.

Seven components have equal base weight: S human satisfaction/confidence; P verified behavior and regressions; A delivery against frozen committed scope; C handoff/review reliability; E corrective-work/flow efficiency; execution-time efficiency; token efficiency. Activity volume is diagnostic, never rewarded. Keep E distinct from raw token/time economy. Use a brief optional sprint human rating as explicitly inherited context, with ticket override; never infer satisfaction from agent prose. Document which signals are direct measures versus product proxies. This is Dark Mechanicus's SPACE-informed policy, not an official SPACE formula.
